document_check.note: The document is Pappalettera C, Nucci L, Cacciotti A, et al. 'Electroencephalography-based signatures of cognitive resilience in individuals with stable mild cognitive impairment despite carrying a high-risk for progression to dementia', Alzheimer's Dement (TRCI) 2025;11:e70194, doi 10.1002/trc2.70194. It is an INTERCEPTOR sub-study comparing baseline resting eyes-closed 19-channel EEG in 60 sMCI-resilient, 56 cMCI (both positive for hippocampal atrophy plus FDG-PET hypometabolism) and 50 healthy controls (Table 1, p.6). The cited small-world numbers are on p.8: 'in the Delta, the HC have lower SW values compared to both sMCI-resilient (p = 0.0038) and cMCI (p = 0.0008), as well as higher Beta 2 SW respect to the other groups (sMCI-resilient [p = 0.0033], cMCI [p = 0.0099])'. This matches the cited result.

cited_result: Small-world (SW) index in 50 healthy controls against two biomarker-selected high-risk MCI groups (60 sMCI-resilient, 56 cMCI), tested by a group x frequency-band mixed ANOVA with Duncan post hoc tests (p.8). Delta band: HC lower than sMCI-resilient (p = 0.0038) and cMCI (p = 0.0008). Beta 2 band: HC higher than sMCI-resilient (p = 0.0033) and cMCI (p = 0.0099). The review sets this against relative beta power, for which no group difference is reported (p.5, p.9).
tool_reason: The cited result compares a baseline EEG network measure (SW index) between healthy controls and MCI groups at one time point, which is a between-group comparison of a biomarker level, not a model, an accuracy estimate or a prognostic association (the 36-month outcome only defines the two MCI subgroups, and HC differ from both in the same direction). Because the controls were recruited separately from the cases, the JBI case-control checklist could also be argued; the review's rule assigns biomarker-in-MCI-versus-controls comparisons to the analytical cross-sectional checklist.

domains.domain: Item 1: Criteria for inclusion clearly defined
domains.rationale: The MCI groups are defined in the text by NIA-AA MCI plus positivity for hippocampal atrophy and FDG-PET hypometabolism, but the positivity cut-offs and all inclusion and exclusion criteria are deferred to the supplement. No eligibility criteria for the healthy controls are given in the document.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined in the document?
signalling.quote: Inclusion and exclusion criteria can be found in the Supplementary Materials.

signalling.question: Were the criteria defining the two high-risk MCI groups stated?
signalling.quote: sMCI-resilient: stable MCI individuals positive for the biomarker combination associated with the highest conversion risk.

signalling.question: Were the biomarker positivity thresholds given in the document?
signalling.quote: For biomarker combinations, positivity (see Table S1) was defined using an AND logic operator, meaning participants had to be positive for all biomarkers in the combination to be included.

signalling.question: Were eligibility criteria for the healthy controls stated?
signalling.quote: A group of 50 healthy controls (HC) recruited outside the Interceptor project was included specifically to provide a comparative benchmark.

domains.domain: Item 2: Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: Demographic, lifestyle and MMSE characteristics are tabulated by group. The setting is described only as the national INTERCEPTOR project, with no recruitment centres or period named, and the source and setting of the externally recruited controls are not described at all.

signalling.question: Were participant characteristics described by group?
signalling.quote: The demographic and lifestyle characteristics and relative p-value are shown in Table 1.

signalling.question: Was the MCI recruitment setting described (centres, period)?
signalling.quote: This work was conducted within the Interceptor Project, which enrolled MCI participants and followed them for 3 years.

signalling.question: Was the recruitment source and setting of the healthy controls described?
signalling.quote: A group of 50 healthy controls (HC) recruited outside the Interceptor project was included specifically to provide a comparative benchmark.

domains.domain: Item 3: Exposure (diagnostic group membership) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: MCI participants had a full biomarker work-up and six-monthly neuropsychology. How the controls were established as cognitively healthy is not stated beyond an MMSE value in Table 1, and there is no indication they received the same assessment (no biomarkers are reported for them).

signalling.question: Was MCI group membership established in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: At baseline, all MCI participants underwent a comprehensive biomarker assessment, which included:

signalling.question: Was follow-up status (which splits the MCI sample) assessed systematically?
signalling.quote: Neuropsychological evaluations were performed every 6 months to assess the main cognitive domains and support the determination of conversion to dementia.

signalling.question: Was healthy status established in the same way for the controls?
signalling.quote: Healthy: cognitively healthy older adults matched for age, sex, and education.

domains.domain: Item 4: Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition
domains.rationale: MCI is defined by the NIA-AA workgroup criteria. The criteria used to diagnose conversion to dementia are not named in the document, but for the HC contrast both MCI subgroups differ from controls in the same direction, so this matters little for the cited result.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for the condition (MCI)?
signalling.quote: The core criteria for MCI diagnosis were defined according to the National Institute on Aging Alzheimer’s Association workgroups.

signalling.question: Were the diagnostic criteria for conversion to dementia named?
signalling.quote: participants converted to a clinical diagnosis of AD and 19 (5.4%) progressed to other clinically defined forms of dementia

domains.rationale: Age, sex, education, family history, smoking and baseline cognition are named as potential influences on the EEG metrics, the family-history and smoking imbalances are recognised, and vascular burden and comorbidity are acknowledged as unmodelled. Medication affecting the EEG is not mentioned.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: Before performing the EEG analyses, Pearson’s correlation analyses were carried out to assess whether demographic and clinical variables influenced the EEG metrics.

signalling.question: Were group imbalances recognised?
signalling.quote: A significant difference was observed for family history of dementia and smoking habits.

signalling.question: Were other factors that affect the EEG (comorbidity, vascular burden, medication) considered?
signalling.quote: the influence of additional biological factors such as vascular burden or other comorbidities was not explicitly modeled in the EEG analyses and could contribute to interindividual variability

domains.domain: Item 6: Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated
domains.rationale: Matching of controls on age, sex and education is asserted but the procedure is not described (Table 1 shows only non-significant differences). The SW mixed ANOVA includes no covariates, so the family-history and smoking imbalances are not addressed in the cited analysis. A covariate-adjusted multiple regression appears only in the Discussion, is not described in the Methods, and its results are not reported for the SW index.

signalling.question: Was a design strategy (matching) stated and described?
signalling.quote: Their EEG profiles were also compared to those of a control group of 50 cognitively healthy older adults, matched for age, sex, and education.

signalling.question: Was the SW comparison adjusted for confounders?
signalling.quote: A mixed-model analysis of variance (ANOVA) was performed with group (healthy, sMCI-resilient, and cMCI) as a between-subject factor and frequency band (delta, theta, alpha 1, alpha 2, beta 1, beta 2, and gamma) as a within-subject factor for the SW analyses.

signalling.question: Is the adjusted analysis claimed in the Discussion described in the Methods and reported for the SW index?
signalling.quote: Initially, a multiple regression analysis including all covariates was carried out. Results suggested that, although some trends are observable, the majority of EEG features were robust enough to the potential confounding effects such as age, sex, education, family history, and baseline cognitive performance.

domains.domain: Item 7: Outcome (SW index) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: The acquisition protocol is standardised (19 channels, eyes closed, at least 5 minutes, at least 3 minutes clean). The SW computation (network construction, thresholding, normalisation) is deferred to the supplement. The document does not say whether the externally recruited controls were recorded with the same equipment and setting as the MCI participants, or whether processing was blind to group. Band limits are inconsistent across the report, including for delta.

signalling.question: Was the EEG acquisition protocol standardised?
signalling.quote: Each participant underwent resting-state EEG recordings in an eyes-closed condition (EC) for at least 5 min using 19 electrodes, positioned according to the International 10–20 System.

signalling.question: Is the SW index computation described in the document?
signalling.quote: The detailed methodologies for the EEG metrics are described in the Supplementary Materials.

signalling.question: Were the externally recruited controls recorded with the same equipment and setting as the MCI participants?
signalling.quote: Searched Methods 2.1 and 2.2 for recording sites, equipment and harmonisation for the HC recruited outside the Interceptor project; none reported.

signalling.question: Was EEG processing blind to group membership?
signalling.quote: Searched Methods 2.2 and 2.3 for blinding of EEG processing; none reported.

signalling.question: Are the frequency-band definitions consistent across the report?
signalling.quote: delta (2–4 Hz), theta (4–8 Hz), alpha 1 (8–11 Hz), alpha 2 (11–13 Hz)

domains.rationale: The omnibus test that gates the cited post hoc comparisons is reported with mutually inconsistent statistics: F(6, 672) = 2.3572 corresponds to p of about 0.029, not 0.00001, and the degrees of freedom fit neither a three-group by seven-band interaction (12 numerator df) nor 166 participants (978 error df); 672 error df imply about 115 participants. The analysis as reported therefore cannot be matched to the stated sample. Post hoc testing used Duncan's multiple range test, which does not control family-wise error, across seven bands and three groups with no further correction. The SW group means and dispersion are only in the supplement, and no covariates were included.

signalling.question: Is the omnibus test internally consistent with its degrees of freedom, p value and sample?
signalling.quote: all factors (F[6, 672] = 2.3572, p = 0.00001), indicating that the SW index differs between the three groups across different EEG frequency bands.

signalling.question: Was multiplicity controlled for the post hoc comparisons across seven bands and three groups?
signalling.quote: When significant main effects or interactions were observed, Duncan post hoc tests for multiple comparisons were applied.

signalling.question: Are the SW group means and dispersion reported in the document?
signalling.quote: SW values (mean ± standard error) for each frequency band (delta, theta, alpha 1, alpha 2, beta 1, beta 2, and gamma) in healthy, sMCI-resilient, and cMCI groups are reported in Table S13.

overall: High risk of bias (JBI analytical cross-sectional: item 8 No; items 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7 Unclear; items 4 and 5 Yes)
overall_rationale: By the review's rule, a No on appropriate statistical analysis gives high risk. The group by band ANOVA that licenses the cited Duncan comparisons is reported with an F value, degrees of freedom and p value that are mutually inconsistent and do not fit the 166 participants analysed, and Duncan's procedure leaves multiplicity across seven bands and three groups uncontrolled. The SW comparison is unadjusted although family history and smoking differ between groups, and the adjustment mentioned in the Discussion is neither described nor reported for SW. The controls were recruited outside the project with no stated eligibility criteria, assessment or recording setting, and the SW computation is only in the supplement, which adds unclear ratings on items 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7.

applicability.rationale: Both MCI groups are a biomarker-selected high-risk subgroup (hippocampal atrophy plus FDG-PET hypometabolism, 116 of 351) of an Italian multicentre MCI cohort, split by 36-month outcome; the controls come from an undescribed source outside the project. The HC contrast does not describe unselected MCI.
Scalp-level 19-channel resting eyes-closed EEG with a band-wise SW index; the network construction is not described in the document and band limits differ between sections.
